battle.name: 宋攻謝晦之戰
battle.brief: 元嘉二十三年（426）正月，荊州刺史謝晦奉密詔舉兵，自江陵、豫章順流而下，二月進抵採石磯，以鐵鎖橫江阻絕舟師。撫軍將軍柳元景以數千之眾守採石，遣蒙衝撞斷鐵鎖，叛軍不能渡。相持數月，疾疫且糧道不繼，謝晦焚舟夜退，兵潰於湘中。前拒所用大楯，與卡面羅馬方陣盾的凸面長盾同源。

kit.name: 羅馬方陣盾
kit.history: 凸面的長方盾。羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚。

countries: 交戰的一方是劉宋朝廷：皇帝宋文帝劉義隆坐鎮建康，以中書令、尚書僕射等制府諸臣參贊機務，遣撫軍將軍柳元景率京師宿衛及揚州、徐州調來的部曲東出拒叛，輔國將軍臧質率眾接應，宿騎名將檀道濟屯廣陵一線截其北竇，豫州刺史沈慶之等分道追擊；朝中則由彭城王劉義康以丞相、錄尚書事、撫軍將軍總攬尚書省，調度荊、襄、雍、豫、徐諸州的人力與糧秣。另一方是荊州軍節度使謝晦所領的叛軍：謝晦時任荊州刺史、都督荊州諸軍事，鎮江陵，與弟豫章刺史謝瑗、荊州長史鄧璞等合謀，以私屬部曲為骨幹，裹脅沿江郡縣的丁夫與被徵發的民力，遣使遊說徐州刺史檀道濟、雍州刺史劉道賜同叛，遊說不成而事洩，遂擁兵東向。荊州地處上游，兵精糧足又擅水軍，自劉裕開國以來便是建康朝廷最不放心的重鎮；朝廷一方則握有江北雍、豫、徐、青諸州的資源與北府兵的老底子，兵力結構是精銳騎兵在北、步卒與水軍在南。叛軍以一州之力挑戰天下，格局上本已不利，而水軍一旦離開江陵上溯，糧秣與兵力的接續便全押在江面一條水道上。
countriesEn: The two sides in this campaign were the Liu Song court at Jiankang and the rebel army raised in Jingzhou. On the government side, Emperor Wen of Song, Liu Yilong, governed from the capital with the Zhongshu Ling, the Shangshu Puye and the other ministry officials deciding policy and executing orders. He sent the Fuwu Jiangjun Liu Yuanjing out of Jiankang with the capital garrison and detachments drawn from Yangzhou and Xuzhou to meet the rebels, with the Fuguo Jiangjun Zang Zhi bringing up the second wave of the army, while the celebrated cavalry commander Tan Daoji was posted on the Guangling line to shut off the northern approach. Behind them the court itself was dominated by the Pengcheng Prince Liu Yikang, who as chancellor and Recorder of the Secretariat controlled the Secretariat and the dispatch of men and grain from Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yu and Xu. The rebel side was the household army of Xie Hui, Governor of Jingzhou and Commander of the Jingzhou Circuit, who was based at Jiangling and acted together with his younger brother Xie Yuan, appointed Governor of Yuzhang, and with Deng Pu, Changshi of Jingzhou. His force was built from his own private troops, the provincial garrison and the men and the drafted labour he could compel from the counties along the river. Messengers went north to win over Tan Daoji, Governor of Xuzhou, and Liu Daci, Governor of Yong. The strategic balance was already against the rebels. Jingzhou was an upstream stronghold with a trained army, a good river fleet and its own supply base, but it stood against the resources of the whole realm and against a capital that still commanded the veteran Northern Army units, the best cavalry in the north and the land and water forces of the lower Yangtze. A single province challenging the whole realm was the losing side of the strategic picture from the start, and once the rebel army left Jiangling and moved upstream, the feeding and reinforcement of that army depended entirely on one water route.
people: 宋文帝劉義隆是全役的樞紐。元嘉二十二年，太子劉劭弒逆弒母，伏誅後劉義隆以平亂登極，旋即以庶弟彭城王劉義康為丞相、錄尚書事、撫軍將軍，總攬朝綱，而劉義隆本人優游少斷，事無大小皆付之義康，義康因此兼握軍政。劉義康的胞妹張皇后正是在那場宮變中遇害，劉義隆的兩位姊姊彭城長公主與廣陵長公主又都站在義康對立面，宮中與宗室的怨望已積到無法收拾。直至元嘉二十三年正月，劉義隆才派中書舍人劉顯齎密詔赴荊州，令謝晦等以誅劉義康為名舉兵入京；事後他把這場兵變寫成清除權臣的非常之舉。諸將之中，撫軍將軍柳元景是採石的主帥，率眾西上拒守，遣死士駕蒙衝撞斷叛軍橫江的鐵鎖，穩住江防；輔國將軍臧質繼至，追擊過於銳進，被詔切責而召回，改由員外散騎侍郎沈慶之接替追擊，終於迫得謝瑗自盡於廬陵、鄱陽一線。徐州刺史檀道濟被謝晦遣使遊說，假意應允，行至廣陵聞朝廷戒嚴才折返建康，叛事平後卻因功高震主被劉義隆賜死，臨刑擲下兜鍪，怒罵「乃壞汝萬里長城」。荊州刺史謝晦自任都督、領兵東下，兵敗逃至襄陽不為雍州刺史劉道賜所納，終為襄陽郡人段虎所殺，傳首建康。謝氏宗族因此連坐流徙，族中才子謝靈運已於元嘉二十年因文讖事被賜死。
peopleEn: Emperor Wen of Song, Liu Yilong, was the pivot of the whole affair. In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia the crown prince Liu Shao rebelled and murdered his mother; after the usurper was put to death Liu Yilong took the throne in the course of suppressing the coup, and he promptly set his half-brother, the Pengcheng Prince Liu Yikang, up as chancellor, Recorder of the Secretariat and Fuwu Jiangjun, so that the whole of government fell into Yikang's hands while the emperor himself remained easygoing and indecisive, referring every matter to his brother. Yikang's own full sister, Empress Zhang, had been one of the murdered in the palace coup, and the emperor's two elder sisters, the Princess of Pengcheng and the Princess of Guangling, both stood against Yikang; resentment in the palace and among the imperial clan had therefore reached the point of no return. Only in the first month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia did Liu Yilong finally act: he sent the Zhongshu sheshi Liu Xian with a secret edict to Jingzhou, ordering Xie Hui and his colleagues to raise an army and enter the capital on the pretext of removing Liu Yikang; afterwards the emperor dressed the rising up as an exceptional measure taken to clear out a usurping minister. Of the generals, the Fuwu Jiangjun Liu Yuanjing commanded at Caishi. He went west with his troops to hold the crossing, and sent shock troops with a covered barge to ram and break the iron chain the rebels had stretched across the river, which kept the river defence in hand. The Fuguo Jiangjun Zang Zhi came up with the second echelon, pressed the pursuit too hard, was sharply reprimanded by an imperial rescript and recalled, and the officer who took over the chase was Shen Qingzhi, Gentleman of the Household Cavalry; he forced Xie Yuan to take his own life at Luling on the Poyang side. Tan Daoji, Governor of Xuzhou, was solicited by Xie Hui and pretended to join, turning back at Guangling only when he heard that the capital had been put on a war footing; once the rising was over he was executed by Liu Yilong for his excessive renown, and as he died he threw down his helmet and cursed that the emperor was destroying his own long wall. Xie Hui himself, Governor of Jingzhou and commander of the army, led the force east and, after his defeat, fled north to Xiangyang, where the Governor of Yong, Liu Daci, refused to receive him; he was finally killed by a man of Xiangyang commandery, Duan Hu, and his head was sent to Jiankang. The Xie clan was punished with banishment and exile, the gifted writer of the family, Xie Lingyun, having already been put to death in the twentieth year of Yuanjia on a charge of writing innuendo.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬方陣盾，是公元前一世紀末羅馬步兵的標準裝備：凸面長方形面板，內設中央鐵握把，邊緣以鐵包箍，戰士以左前臂套入繫帶、右手握把，雙手推盾前進，盾緣彼此咬合成線。它要抵擋的是標槍、投石與騎兵衝撞，重點在讓整排人的力量合成一面牆，而不是盾本身多厚。與它同源而不同形者，是劉宋軍中的所謂大楯：戰國以來楚、秦的巨型長盾可容數人並立，宋軍仍以各式盾為步兵常備，但已是兩晉南渡後的樣貌——前排精兵持大楯結陣抵擋，後列以環首刀、長槊戳刺，弓弩擔任主要火力，兜鍪與札甲蔽護身體。所謂前拒，就是以大楯列陣擋住敵軍的第一次衝撞，讓後方弩手不受干擾地射擊。決定這場戰爭勝負的裝備並不是盾牌，而是弩與水戰器材：叛軍在江心拉鐵鎖橫江，又備火船打算順風焚燒朝方舟師；宋軍則以蒙衝、斗艦、艟艦結陣，用載有薪柴的蒙衝撞斷鐵鎖，打通航道。野戰另備大槊、鉤、鐓與木製拒馬，攻城則有木樓與雲梯。糧秣靠江陵、襄陽沿漢水沮漳一線北運，逆流一段便要換船數次，遇上春汛與逆風便停滯不進。
kitsEn: The Roman scutum on the card face was the standard equipment of Roman infantry in the last century before the era: a convex rectangular shield face with an iron grip in the middle and iron bindings along the rim, carried by a soldier who slipped his left forearm into the strap and gripped the handle with the right hand, pushing the shield ahead with both hands so that neighbouring rims locked edge to edge. It was built to withstand javelins, sling stones and the impact of charging cavalry, and the point of the design was to let a whole rank add its strength into one continuous wall rather than to make any single shield thick. The Chinese counterpart, and the relative of the same family, was the da dun of Liu Song: the huge long shields of Chu and Qin in the Warring States could shelter several men abreast, and Song infantry still carried shields of every shape as standard kit, but by then, after the crossing of the river and the move south of the two Jin, the form had changed. Front-rank picked men braced the line with large shields, the ranks behind thrust with ring-pommel sabres and long lances, bows and crossbows supplied the main volume of fire, and helmets and lamellar armour protected the body. What the troops called the forward refusal, the front line of shields, was exactly this: large shields held in a row to absorb the first impact of the enemy so that the crossbowmen behind could shoot undisturbed. The equipment that actually decided this war was not the shield but the crossbow and the river craft. The rebels stretched iron chains across the middle of the river and prepared fire ships to burn the government flotilla downwind. The Song side massed covered barges, fighting galleys and light swift vessels, and used a covered barge loaded with brushwood to ram and snap the chains, opening the channel. In the field the troops carried long lances, hooks, spear shafts and wooden trip devices, and for sieges they had wooden towers and ladders. Grain came up from Jiangling and Xiangyang along the Han and the middle Yangtze, and every stretch of upstream water meant another change of boat; when the spring floods and adverse winds came, the movement stopped dead.
tactics: 這是一場典型的上游重鎮叛軍試圖順流而下、直取下游首都的戰役。謝晦據江陵，先遣謝瑗自豫章取道鄱陽、彭澤，企圖由南面包抄建康；主力則沿長江西上，兵鋒直指採石磯——此處江面收束、兩岸石壁陡峭，是從上游進入下游的咽喉要道。柳元景先一步據採石，以數千之眾築壘自守，又把可用於渡兵的江面收束到極窄，逼叛軍必須走水上的唯一通道。叛軍在江心拉起鐵鎖橫江，形成一道水下的阻斷線；柳元景不與之硬拼，先遣死士駕著蒙衝，船上堆積薪草，順流撞擊，斷其鎖而過，隨後全軍鼓行渡江，反過來在北岸築壘，與叛軍隔水相持。朝廷的戰略是三部並行：柳元景正面拒守於採石，檀道濟率精騎屯廣陵切斷叛軍北路，臧質、沈慶之等分兵追擊南北兩翼，使謝晦無法合兵。叛軍的失誤在於把戰場壓成一條狹窄水道上的死結：重兵集於江面，後方空虛，糧秣須由江陵逆流而上，一遇逆風逆水便停滯；久屯江畔，士卒泡在水與泥中，營中大疫流行，兵氣與糧道同時崩壞，最後只能焚舟夜退，把主動權全部交回朝廷。
tacticsEn: This was a textbook attempt by an upstream provincial command to march down the river and strike at the capital of the lower reaches. Holding Jiangling, Xie Hui first sent Xie Yuan out of Yuzhang by way of Poyang and Pengze, hoping to encircle Jiankang from the south, while the main body went up the Yangtze with its point aimed at Caishi, where the river narrows between steep rock banks and forms the throat through which any army from the upper reaches must pass to enter the lower river. Liu Yuanjing reached Caishi first, raised his camp with several thousand men and held it, at the same time narrowing to the smallest possible the stretch of water through which the enemy could cross, forcing the rebels onto the single river route. The rebels then ran iron chains across the middle of the river, forming a barrier below the surface. Liu Yuanjing did not try to force it by strength. He sent shock troops down in covered barges loaded with brushwood, let them drift with the current and ram the chains until they snapped, then beat the gongs and marched the whole army over, turned the position and built a camp on the north bank to hold the rebels at the river. The strategy of the court worked on three fronts at once: Liu Yuanjing held the front at Caishi, Tan Daoji kept his picked cavalry at Guangling to close the northern road, and Zang Zhi, Shen Qingzhi and others pursued the southern and northern wings in turn, so that Xie Hui could never concentrate his forces. The rebels' mistake was to compress the whole battle into a deadlock on one narrow waterway. Their strength was piled up on the river while their rear lay empty, and their grain had to be dragged up from Jiangling against the current, so that any adverse wind or water stopped the column. Camping for months on the river bank left the troops standing in water and mud, disease ran through the camp, and morale and supply broke down together, until the only thing left was to burn the boats and slip away by night, handing the initiative back to the court.
data: 兵力數字多有誇大，正史只給概略。叛軍方面，謝晦自江陵發動時可用的核心是荊州宿兵與其私屬部曲，史稱以荊州之眾，總數當在數萬之譜；謝瑗在豫章另領一軍，兩部相加仍不過上游一州之地。朝廷方面，柳元景初至採石的兵只有數千人，多為京師宿衛與揚州、徐州調來的部曲；其後臧質、沈慶之等率眾接應，檀道濟的精騎屯於廣陵一線，加上雍、豫、徐、青諸州奉詔北上的援軍，總數遠勝叛軍，但到達需時，難以及時合圍。時間上，元嘉二十三年正月謝晦舉兵，二月即抵採石磯，隨即被阻；兩軍隔江相持數月，至是年夏秋間疫病大起、糧道斷絕，謝晦才焚舟退去，宋軍追擊至湘中一帶收束戰事。戰線自江陵至建康為數百里水路，叛軍全程在水上與兩岸縱列前進，糧船要逆溯漢水、沮漳一線，運量與速度都受限制。器械方面可確定的只有橫江鐵鎖、蒙衝、薪柴、弩與大楯等種類，具體數目史無明文；雙方陣亡與被俘的數字歷來不詳，這場戰役沒有留下可信的傷亡統計，可核者只有年月、官職、地名與兵器的種類。
dataEn: The strength figures are largely exaggerated and the official histories give only a general sense. On the rebel side the core available to Xie Hui when he moved from Jiangling was the Jingzhou garrison together with his private troops, described in the sources simply as the Jingzhou men; the total can hardly have been less than several thousand and probably stood in the tens of thousands at most, and Xie Yuan led a separate force from Yuzhang, so that even together the two columns amounted to no more than the resources of a single upstream province. On the government side Liu Yuanjing had only several thousand men when he first reached Caishi, mostly the capital garrison and detachments called out from Yangzhou and Xuzhou; Zang Zhi, Shen Qingzhi and the others brought up the second and third waves, Tan Daoji kept his picked cavalry on the line of Guangling, and contingents from Yong, Yu, Xu and Qing marched north on the imperial summons, so that the government fielded far more men than the rebels, though the march took time and no encirclement could be made at once. As to time, Xie Hui rose in the first month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia and was at Caishi in the second, where he was checked immediately; the two armies held opposite banks of the river for several months, and only when disease broke out in the summer and autumn of that year and the supply line failed did Xie Hui burn his boats and withdraw, with the Song pursuit closing the action in the region of Xiangzhong. The front ran for several hundred li of river from Jiangling to Jiankang, and the rebels moved the whole way in column on the water and along the banks, with the grain boats having to be hauled upstream along the Han and the middle Yangtze, so that both the volume carried and the speed of movement were limited. As for equipment, the only items securely attested are the iron chains across the river, the covered barges, the brushwood, crossbows and large shields; no reliable counts of any of them survive in the records. Figures for casualties and prisoners are simply not available: this campaign left no trustworthy casualty statistics, and only the dates, the official ranks, the place names and the kinds of weapons can be checked.
cause: 起因有三層。第一層是權力：元嘉二十二年太子劉劭弒逆弒母被誅後，劉義隆以庶弟彭城王劉義康為丞相、錄尚書事、撫軍將軍，朝政與軍權盡歸一身，自己只剩下名號。第二層是血緣與姻親積下的舊怨：劉義康的胞妹張皇后死於那場宮變，劉義隆的兩位姊姊又都與義康不睦，宮中與宗室的怨望已積到無法收拾。第三層是文帝對上游的恐懼。劉宋立國以來，揚州、荊州、徐州三鎮分握重兵，文帝自劉裕遺制，時刻提防地方都督；荊州刺史謝晦與徐州刺史檀道濟都是坐鎮上游的大將，聲望並高，義康在朝中又力主削抑上游兵權，元嘉二十三年遂傳出收二人兵權、追奪封邑的訊息。謝晦自知大禍臨頭，卻在密詔到家之後，發現已經無路可退：詔書既出於皇帝，順詔舉兵尚可自居為勤王，一旦朝廷平叛，叛軍所挾的名分立刻化為笑柄，討伐的對象便只剩叛軍本身。於是謝晦據江陵，與弟謝瑗、長史鄧璞合謀，分兵東指，遣使遊說上游與北方的同寅，準備以一州之眾問鼎建康。
causeEn: The causes work on three levels. The first is power: after the crown prince Liu Shao was put to death for the murder of his mother in the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, Liu Yilong made his half-brother the Pengcheng Prince Liu Yikang chancellor, Recorder of the Secretariat and Fuwu Jiangjun, and the whole of government and the command of the army passed to Yikang, leaving the emperor with nothing but a title. The second layer is old resentment stored up in blood and marriage: Yikang's own full sister, Empress Zhang, was killed in that palace coup, and the emperor's two elder sisters were both at odds with Yikang, so that ill will in the palace and among the imperial clan had grown past the point of repair. The third layer is the emperor's fear of the upper river. Since the founding of the dynasty the three circuits of Yangzhou, Jingzhou and Xuzhou had each held heavy troops, and following the precedent of Liu Yu the emperors were forever on guard against a regional commander with troops in his hand. Xie Hui, Governor of Jingzhou, and Tan Daoji, Governor of Xuzhou, were both great commanders sitting on the upper river with high renown, and Yikang in the capital pressed hard to reduce the military power of the upper provinces, so that by the twenty-third year of Yuanjia there were reports that the two men were to be stripped of their commands and of their fiefs. When the secret edict reached Xie Hui he understood that his ruin was at hand and that there was no way back: since the edict came from the emperor, obeying it could still be dressed up as service to the throne, but once the court had beaten the rising the pretext would turn to laughter, and the only party left to be attacked would be the rebels themselves. So Xie Hui held Jiangling, took counsel with his brother Xie Yuan and the Changshi Deng Pu, split his forces to march east, and sent messengers to sound out his colleagues on the upper river and in the north, preparing to challenge Jiankang with the resources of one province.
impact: 此役的意義遠超一場上游兵變。第一，劉宋的上游防範政策暫時奏效，而代價是人頭落地：元嘉二十三年八月，文帝以誣上、專恣之罪殺檀道濟，收其妻子資財，檀道濟死前把兜鍪擲於地，怒罵「乃壞汝萬里長城」，此事成為南北朝自毀長城的典型案例；朝廷此後對將領的猜忌更甚，荊、揚、徐州的都督更替頻仍，北伐的兵力基礎由此受損。第二，劉義康失勢：罷丞相、錄尚書事，貶為豫章王，幽於吳郡，元嘉二十五年仍被賜死，劉義隆終於為自己的遲疑付出代價，兄弟之間的信任就此破裂。第三，謝氏門第覆滅，陳郡謝氏自東晉以來數代掌軍政的傳統中斷，謝靈運一系的文名與鄉里根基一併摧折。第四，江南不戰而保，長江天險與採石一線的地形價值被重新確認，此後南北對峙，採石始終是下游渡江與防守的必爭咽喉。第五，軍制層面上，朝廷在戰後更細密地分割荊、雍諸州、削損都督權力，換用外人鎮守要地，使上游不再集中足以叛亂的資源，這一安排延續到南朝末年，是南朝得以在江左苟安的基本前提之一。
impactEn: The meaning of this campaign reaches far beyond an uprising in an upstream province. First, the policy of guarding against the upper river had a temporary success, and the price was paid in heads: in the eighth month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia the emperor put Tan Daoji to death for slandering the throne and for his own arrogant power, confiscating his wives, children and goods. As he died Tan Daoji threw down his helmet and cried out that the emperor was destroying his own long wall; the incident became the standard example of a state tearing down its own defences in the southern and northern courts. The court's suspicion of its commanders deepened afterwards, the commanders of Jing, Yang and Xu were turned over with great frequency, and the military basis of the northern expeditions was damaged accordingly. Second, Liu Yikang fell: he was stripped of the chancellorship and the Recordership of the Secretariat, demoted to Prince of Yuzhang, shut up in Wujun, and was still put to death in the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, so that Liu Yilong finally paid for his own long indecision and trust between the emperor and his brother was broken for good. Third, the Xie house was destroyed; the Chenjun Xie clan, which had held military and political power for several generations since the Eastern Jin, was broken as a governing house, and with it went the literary fame of the Xie line and the standing of the clan in its home county. Fourth, the south of the river was saved without a battle, and the value of the Yangtze barrier and of the line at Caishi was reconfirmed; from then on, in every later stand between north and south, Caishi remained the throat through which a crossing of the lower river had to be forced or held. Fifth, at the level of military administration, the court divided Jing, Yong and the neighbouring provinces yet more finely after the war and cut down the authority of the circuit commanders, posting outsiders to the key commands so that the upper river no longer held resources sufficient for a rising; this arrangement ran on to the end of the Southern Dynasties and was one of the basic preconditions of the survival of the southern court on the left bank of the river.
result: 結果是叛軍全線覆滅，朝廷以建康不驚而全勝。謝晦主力在採石被柳元景所阻，無法渡江，僵持數月後疫病大起、糧道斷絕，遂焚舟夜退；宋軍乘勝追擊，臧質追至湘中，因進兵過速被詔召回，改由沈慶之接手，迫得謝瑗在廬陵、鄱陽一線服毒自盡，鄧璞在江陵兵敗自盡。謝晦本人北走襄陽，雍州刺史劉道賜不納，終為襄陽郡人段虎所殺，首級傳送建康。朝廷的處置隨即展開：劉義康罷相、貶為豫章王、幽於吳郡；檀道濟以戰功震主，於同年八月被誅，籍沒家產；謝氏宗族及與之往來者多坐流徙，陳郡謝氏在軍政上的一門勢力從此退場。從戰役本身的技術層面看，決定勝負的是三件事：採石的地形與柳元景的據守、叛軍水戰器材的粗糙——鐵鎖橫江雖能阻船，卻擋不住載薪的蒙衝衝撞——以及叛軍糧秣必須逆流北上這一致命弱點。北方上游的軍鎮在這場戰役中既沒有被朝廷坐收，也沒有被叛軍穩住，劉宋此後仍須在用上游兵與防上游叛之間反覆權衡。
resultEn: The result was the complete destruction of the rebel army and a complete victory for the court without alarm in Jiankang. The main body of Xie Hui was stopped at Caishi by Liu Yuanjing and could not cross; after months of stalemate, disease broke out and the supply line failed, and he burned his boats and withdrew by night. The Song army pursued: Zang Zhi chased as far as Xiangzhong, was recalled by imperial rescript for advancing too fast, and Shen Qingzhi took over, forcing Xie Yuan to take his own life at Luling on the Poyang side, while Deng Pu died by his own hand at Jiangling after the defeat there. Xie Hui himself fled north to Xiangyang, where Liu Daci, Governor of Yong, would not take him in, and he was killed at last by Duan Hu of Xiangyang commandery, his head being carried to Jiankang. The disposal of the matter followed at once: Liu Yikang was stripped of the chancellorship, demoted to Prince of Yuzhang and shut up in Wujun; Tan Daoji, whose great services had made him a source of dread, was executed in the eighth month of the same year and his property confiscated; the Xie clan and those who had kept company with them were sentenced to banishment and exile, and the Xie house as a governing clan in the military and the state retired from the stage. As for the technical side of the campaign itself, three things decided the outcome: the ground at Caishi and the way Liu Yuanjing held it; the crudeness of the rebel river equipment, for although the iron chains could hold ships back they could not stop a covered barge loaded with brushwood from ramming them; and the fatal weakness of a rebel army whose grain had to be moved upstream against the current. The military commands of the upper river were neither recovered by the court nor secured by the rebels in this war, and the Liu Song state would go on weighing the same balance for a long time, between using the troops of the upper river and fearing the revolt of the upper river.
